`/vet-code` Step 3 requires Pass B pinned to the strongest available model. **Opus-pinned sub-agents

round one ran one tier down, flagged as **not** discharging Step 3. Erez then directed: *"fix the confirmed

coding at half the cost. **Erez's call on the record, not the skill's default.**

**Dead end, do not repeat:** retrying a 529'd tier immediately. Five attempts produced nothing. What worked
was running the cheaper tier for breadth and re-running the strong tier later.

**The tier difference was not marginal.** The Opus panel produced nine findings the lower tier missed, *and*
caught two defects inside the lower-tier round's own fixes. Direct evidence for Step 3's tier requirement.

Three cold `check-reviewer` sub-agents per round, each given only the diff, the working file, the suite and
the goal quoted verbatim — with an explicit prohibition on reading any `.md` in `notes/gen508-piece1/`

(new-defect hunt), `ae4fe1e34604338b1` (forgery/replay + adversarial suite audit), `a2b729e891f5fe8e0`
(false premises + contract drift). Round-one and round-two ids are tabulated in the README.

### Rounds one and two — 5 defects fixed (suite 27 -> 38)

- **`findPassInDir` failed OPEN on a pass file containing the literal `null`.** `null` is valid JSON, so the
  reader's try/catch never fired and `pass.expires` threw uncaught — a non-2 exit, which is not a refusal.
  Reproduced live, fixed, re-verified. **This is PRE-EXISTING live code**, shared with the staging, vetting
  and check-due pass dirs, so the fail-open is live in three ALREADY-INSTALLED gates. Now filed as GEN-670.
- The stale wiring comment claiming the gate covers raw REST (it is unwired in piece 1a).
- **Both round-two defects were inside round one's own hash re-assert.** Written as a bare
  `rec.contentHash !== sc.hash`, it was *stricter* than the matcher it re-asserted (`ticketRecordMatches`
  trims and lower-cases), so a record carrying the newline `--ticket-hash` prints matched the finder then
  failed as `bad-record`, whose remedy regenerates an identical record — a closed lockout loop escapable
  only by break-glass. It was also the first dereference of `rec`, and `JSON.parse('null')` succeeds, so it
  moved a crash site *earlier*. One call to `ticketRecordMatches` closed both.
- **The housekeeping exemption was not tool-scoped**, so `notion-duplicate-page` with `{page_id, properties}`
  returned `out` — and a duplicate spawns a live ticket.

token being read from a reviewer's `thinking` blocks and `tool_use` arguments (now an allow-list of `text`
blocks, and "last" now means the final delivered message, grounded in 1,204 of 1,206 real transcripts
ending `assistant [text]`); `ticketSessionDir` resolving one directory too deep for a sub-agent caller;

**The bug-3 fix reached the wrong half, and the review caught it.** The GEN-58 carve-out was fixed to accept

**Second blocking finding, verified live:** the MCP content hash binds the payload and not the tool, so one

## 2026-08-05 (2) — GEN-508 first `/code-review` run (14 findings): four skill/hook format mismatches that would have blocked every ticket write, found and fixed; Erez narrowed the piece to the MCP surface and the raw-REST arm was unwired; the test suite split in two and made runnable for the first time. Nothing installed.
<!-- session:48087e06-5ca4-4eb5-a621-c38e6543febb -->

**Where it started.** Erez asked what effort level GEN-508 needed, then whether to code-review what was already written or keep building. Reading `notes/gen508-piece1/README.md` settled it: the handoff's own "Still open" section put two `/code-review` passes next, before `/vet-code` steps 4–8. He launched the first pass.

### The first `/code-review` pass — 14 findings, 8 fixed this session

Run at xhigh over the 6-hunk, 1,532-line hook diff. The headline cluster: **the v8 hook and the `/vet-ticket` skill disagreed about the record format in four independent ways**, each of which alone hard-blocks every gated Team-Tasks write and leaves break-glass as the only route.

1. The skill minted the pass with `contentHash` nested inside a `targets[]` array; the hook reads `rec.contentHash` at the top level, so no pass it produced could ever match.
2. The skill never told the reviewer to emit `TICKET-REVIEW-VERDICT: PASS <hash>` — v8's central new check, read out of the reviewer's own transcript.
3. The minted pass carried no `verdict`/`waived`; those lived in a `ticket-record` file the hook never opens (no `expires`, so `findPassInDir` skips it).
4. The skill recorded plural `reviewerAgentIds`; the hook reads a singular `rec.reviewerAgentId`.

**Why the tests didn't catch it:** `test-gen508-v8-arm.js` builds its pass fixtures to the hook's contract, so they were green while the only sanctioned producer emitted a different shape. Green fixtures did not imply a working gate.

All four fixed in the skill working copy, plus the stale batch-pass description (v8 deleted `targets[]` and partial consumption; `consumePassFile` renames the whole file, so one write retires an entire "batch" pass). Step 1 now hashes **before** the review, because the reviewer must sign the hash.

Also fixed: the `PROTECTED_FILES` entry for `notion-rest-write.ps1` (it blocked the script's own creation, while the adjacent comment claimed creation was silently approved), and a README instruction telling piece 3 to count a `claim-lost` event the hook never emits.

Three findings are unreachable while the REST arm is unwired and are carried on the piece-2 ticket; three remain live and are now GEN-663.

### Erez's decision: piece 1a is the MCP surface only

Asked to choose between shipping the ordinary Notion route now and holding everything until the raw-shortcut route was covered too, he chose **path A**. Deferring had to mean *switching the arm off*, not shipping it: as built it would have refused every raw REST write with no working escape (pinned script not on disk, and the change itself protected that path).

Five attachment points removed — the `isShell` branch in `enforceTicketVetting`, the `--ticket-hash-shell` dispatch, the `-shell` mode of `isSafeTicketHash`, the `PROTECTED_FILES` entry, plus a NOT WIRED banner over §4.5 naming the three preconditions for reconnection. The diff against the live hook stays **purely additive: 1,558 added, 0 removed**, 6 hunks.

Corrected in that banner: §4.5 had claimed raw REST "carries the ONLY destructive operations in the surface." It does not — move-out (which drops every database property), `replace_content` and `allow_deleting_content` are all destructive and all are gated by piece 1a. That false claim had been an argument against deferring.

So the README's "48 assertions, all passing" was not reproducible — the count was right, the run predated a rename. ## 2026-08-04 (3) — GEN-508 piece 1: raw-REST arm covered on Erez's call; five `/check` rounds killed the parse-the-command mechanism, Erez chose to replace it, v8 was designed and reviewed over three more rounds — then (continuing 2026-08-05) **applied** to the design doc, the ticket handoff was rewritten, and the hook working copy was **rebuilt against v8** and re-based after the live hook changed mid-session. **Decision 1 (Erez).** Shown §12.1's three-way scope choice in plain language, he chose **"cover it now"** (Option A) over the standing recommendation (Option B, ship-and-defer): raw REST/curl Notion writes are IN piece 1. **Decision 2 (Erez).** After round 5 he chose **"replace it"** — drop the parse-the-shell-command mechanism rather than patch it a sixth time.

**Decisions 3-5 (Erez, 2026-08-05).** Apply v8 into the normative document; then rewrite the ticket's build-state handoff **first**; then rebuild the working copy **in one pass** rather than splitting it (the reason he was given: half of this flow is not reviewable, since both surfaces share the same back half, so a split buys a smaller review that cannot conclude anything).

### Part 1 — v7: the delta, and five rounds that never converged

**v7 applied as a delta to the single normative document** (`notes/gen508-piece1/design-converged.md`), not a new file — the two-document split was the previous session's round-3 diagnosis. Four changes: new §4.5 (the raw REST/curl arm); the **adjudicator role deleted** (§9 → stub, §6.2 rewritten); the **PostToolUse volume-id appender cut** (deliverable 4); and deliverable 10's fork resolved — `/wrap`'s two filing steps stay **unattended**, with the cost stated.

**`/check`: five rounds, thirteen reviews, never converged.** R1 (Sonnet): holistic PASS, pre-mortem REVISE (5), soundness REVISE (2). R2: soundness cleared both, raised one NEW-FROM-REVISION; pre-mortem cleared four of five. R3 (Opus, cap): soundness PASS, pre-mortem RECURRENCE → escalated. R4 (Opus, 2 lenses, gate 1 only): both REVISE on the same independently-reached finding. R5 (Opus, 3 lenses): **all three REVISE.** Reviewer ids r1 `a7ee238379a4af562`, `aae03ca6224426b82`, `aaa68b8f281947130`; r2 `a99475dd331c499ee`, `acd5e88a491e4a4f0`; r3 `a5cc3ab1a784bee78`, `aee729e4666c6470b`; r4 `ae24c9b5add4b6426`, `a0700fdd0f864ecdc`; r5 `a395787aaf80fb75f`, `a2cf4b4426b649d28`, `a099004b7d33ec47c`.

**The class that recurred five times.** Every round found a different way a raw write reaches Notion carrying a body the record's hash does not cover — i.e. the gate mints a record falsely assuring a reviewer saw bytes they never saw, which is worse than ungated. (1) A PowerShell sub-expression `-Body (Get-Content -Raw x.json)`. (2) An unexpanded variable inside a well-formed argument. (3) A body piped in with no body argument (`scanChain` treats a single `|` as non-chaining, `auto-approve.js:409`-`412`). (4) The "whitelist" was really four *disqualifiers*, so `--data-ascii "@file"`, `-K`/`--config`, `-F`/`--form` and a PS `@props` splat passed and were hashed as bodyless. (5) The round-4 token rule was specified over `scanChain`'s `bare`, returned **only** on `CHAINED` (`:459`; `NO-CHAIN` returns none, `:460`) while gate 1 runs only on `NO-CHAIN` — and which **deletes** quoted spans (`:424`-`:448`). Plus a channel outside the command entirely: curl reads `%USERPROFILE%\.curlrc` unless `-q` is first.

**Round 5's holistic lens asked what five rounds had not — is parsing the command the right mechanism at all?** — and found `auto-approve.js` already answers this class the other way, by recognising a **named invocation form**, with a comment at `:1306`-`:1313` warning that a "*successful but wrong* extraction … could compare equal and fail OPEN". Its proposal: an anchored whole-command template. That went to Erez, who chose replacement.

### Part 2 — v8: the replacement, designed and reviewed

**The round-5 proposal was measured and rejected on the measurement.** An anchored template over the *curl command itself* matches **0 of 236** real raw-REST write commands, and structurally so: 234 of 236 retrieve the Notion token from the Windows Credential Vault **inside the same command**, 176 are 11+ lines, exactly 1 is a single line. There is no token env var, so a single-line curl command cannot authenticate — the template would have made the record path unreachable, i.e. Option C (the funnel) by the back door, which Erez declined.

**v8's mechanism.** Stop trying to understand arbitrary commands. Move the vault retrieval, the client, the headers and the API version **inside one project-owned script**, `~/.claude/scripts/notion-rest-write.ps1` (its full text is in the design), so the gated command is one anchored line with three mandatory slots: `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "<script>" -Method (POST|PATCH|DELETE) -Url "<url>" -BodyFile "<abs path|NONE>"`. Hash = `sha256(stableStringify({surface:"notion-rest", method, url, bodySha}))`. Two branches, no third: the command **references the script by basename anywhere** → must match the template exactly (else hard-block), pin check first, then slots → body → exemption → hash; **otherwise** → the copied detector, and any detected Notion write hard-blocks. This reuses a pattern already live three times in `auto-approve.js` (`isSafeSyncFromClaude`, `isSafeNotionTicketLookup`, `isSafeLoggateTouch` — all anchored `^…$`, no `m` flag). The script's sha256 is **pinned in `auto-approve.js`**, computed from the design's own code block, because new-file creation falls through to a prompt and a prompt is a silent approve under `bypassPermissions` — so only reviewing the text closes the initial contents. Separators are `[ \t]+`, never `\s+` (which matches a newline: an anchored match would then mint and consume a record for a write that never runs).

**Deletes:** gate 1 in full, gate 2 in full, the chain guard and its two reasons, the command-text half of the token clause. **Adds:** one ~40-line script, one anchored recogniser, one sentinel, one pinned hash, one `PROTECTED_FILES` entry.

**Three more `/check` rounds (all Opus). R1 all REVISE; R2 all REVISE; R3 (cap) pre-mortem PASS, holistic PASS, soundness REVISE on one new finding.** Ids r1 `a5520d958283913f5`, `ae95f46cd9937bf80`, `a71332e4fc961d056`; r2 `a47f60f81c99f222e`, `ad9f126606f01dc55`, `a69167658feb1f4f9`; r3 `aaeb67faf37333c26`, `a919b2c8d19b7f5fd`, `a73f6211ea9d9e28a`. Every carried finding from r1/r2 was tagged RESOLVED by its own lens in r3. The r3 finding (the script dropped `-k` while all 236 corpus commands use `-sk`/`-sSk`) was **resolved by evidence, not another revision**: `curl.exe -q -sS … https://api.notion.com/v1/users/me` returned `HTTP=401`, so TLS verification works here and `-k` is habit; the lens's second ask — a **live end-to-end install verification** — is adopted as a blocking install step. No fourth round (the cap).

**The finding that mattered, found independently by all three r1 lenses: v8's own first draft failed open on POST** — the sixth instance of the recurring class, created by my fix. Moving curl into the script removed the only token `HTTP_CLIENT_RE` (`notion-schema-guard.js:131`) requires; POST is absent from both hard write-verb patterns (`:138`, `:139`); `-BodyFile` cannot match `BODY_FLAG_RE`'s `-Body\b` (`:134`). So an assignment-prefixed, `cd`-prefixed, chained or multiline canonical POST invocation was neither prefix-matched nor detected — a **silent approve on a page create**, i.e. filing a ticket. Fixed by the basename-anywhere trigger (the only thing that catches PowerShell parameter abbreviation, `-M/-U/-B`, which carries no `-Method` token at all) plus dropping the client-name gate entirely, and verified by measurement.

**The measurement programme — the session's most reusable output.** Ten scripts, bundled as provenance at `notes/gen508-piece1/v8-measurement-scripts.txt`. Over **1,247** distinct shell commands mentioning `api.notion.com`, the live schema-guard rule flags **242** and the arm's detector (client-name gate dropped, native-call patterns added) flags **242** — **+0**, and it misses **0** of the 236 Part-4a writes. Refusal classes, discriminated by the **write verb** (not the URL): `rest-not-via-script` **210**, `rest-template-cannot-express` **3**, `rest-signal-no-target` **29** — the last being Bash *read* commands whose only write signal is `tr -d '\r'` matching the detector's single-letter `-d`. Two proposed widenings were **measured and rejected**: the every-URL read test (+11 commands, all reads) and dropping `-d` (would remove the 29 over-refusals and lose 0 real writes, but the shape it stops detecting, `curl -d '{…}' <write URL>`, is a real write form). **Correction to the design's own numbers:** 29 of the 233/236/242 counted "writes" are reads, so the raw-REST write population is ~213 and "~15% of write traffic" is simultaneously an overcount and a floor. **The rule this establishes: a widening is measured before adoption, not after.**

**What v8 costs, measured not inferred.** 210 write commands must be reissued through the script; **29 read commands break too** (fix: one token, `tr --delete '\r'`) — and the round-2 draft hid this behind the word "inherited": the *detection* is inherited from the live rule, but that rule emits `ask`, which is inert, so all 29 execute today. 3 commands have no canonical route (must use MCP). **Three live instruction surfaces prescribe the now-refused idiom** — `hooks/refs/notion.md:15` (hook-injected on every Notion-mentioning turn), `skills/notion-howto/SKILL.md:21`, `skills/shell-howto/SKILL.md:30` — so without editing them every raw-REST write begins with a refused command **forever**; they are **ship blockers** alongside `/wrap` Steps 1/3c, which narrows §14's install seam to "hook + skill + the three instruction edits".

## 2026-08-04 (2) — GEN-615 + GEN-620 paired: designed over six /check rounds, built, then TWO code-review rounds (9 defects fixed, 5 still open); NOT installed
<!-- session:bd0001a6-26bf-477d-8189-caeb0b4b2de5 -->
**Ask.** Work GEN-615, find whether another ticket should be done with it, and if so propose a path for both. Session started at medium effort, raised to xhigh for the design and high for the build at Erez's instruction.

### Pairing decision
GEN-615 (two sessions on the same **ticket**) paired with **GEN-620** (two sessions in the same **folder**). Both tickets say not to *merge* them and that still holds — but they are the same machine underneath: same source of truth (the auto-approve edit log), same unresolved id-correlation question, same trigger/staleness design, same awkward two-session test rig. Doing them apart means solving all of that twice. GEN-620 had also already done the measurement work GEN-615 lacked.

GEN-621/GEN-152 were **explicitly not touched**: session 13a207fe was live on them at the time (a real instance of GEN-615's own failure, caught by looking).

### The blocker both tickets named turned out to be a non-issue
GEN-615 said the two id spaces don't line up so any check stays heuristic. True of `list_sessions` (measured: **0 of 200** of its ids intersect the 171 ids in the edit log, and no hook can call an MCP tool anyway) — and irrelevant, because `~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json` shares the edit log's id space exactly. That is an exact join plus a real pid liveness check, which is also what answers the objection that killed advisory locks in GEN-218.

### Design — `notes/gen615-gen620-design/design-v7.md`, six /check rounds
One hook, two events, one liveness reader, two keys. `UserPromptSubmit` → ticket key (self-registering presence map, so no transcript parsing); `PreToolUse` → folder key (the edit log already *is* the folder signal). Awareness only, never blocking, and no CLAUDE.md growth — the "stop and ask" instruction rides inside the injected text.

Six rounds **removed** seven pieces of logic and added self-diagnosis. What each round killed:
- **R1:** a 120-minute folder window (unjustified by its own cited evidence, and a fixed cutoff reintroduced the very TTL-vs-idle-gap mismatch GEN-218 used to reject locking).
- **R2:** a `cwd` filter on the ticket half (GEN ids are global across all three projects, and pruning through a folder-filtered set could delete another project's live registration); a 24-hour map expiry (the same TTL mistake, second instance).
- **R3:** the `procStart` requirement — **measured present in only 1 of 7 live session files**, so requiring it read six of seven live sessions as dead and the hook would have installed clean and done nothing forever. Also removed self-exclusion from the liveness set (each session would have deleted its own registration every prompt).
- **R4:** `procStart` dropped entirely rather than made optional; self-presence became a hard gate; a **lower** monitoring bar added (zero ticket-half firings in three weeks is *suspect*, not reassuring).
- **R5:** `agent_id` added to the dedupe keys — sub-agents carry the parent's `session_id`, so a sub-agent's read was consuming the parent's one-per-folder warning slot and silencing the parent's own read, with no re-arm in the case the design calls the one that matters. This review's own panel was an instance.
- **R6:** a false coverage claim (§7 cited a §6 test the restructure had dropped).

Three of six rounds each caught a defect that would have shipped inert. The design's *shape* never changed after R1. **The panel had escalated at its own 3-round cap; rounds 4–6 happened only because Erez asked for them** — filed as GEN-629.

### Build — `concurrent-session-warn.js` + `test-concurrent-session-warn.js`, 50 tests
Building it falsified two things the reviewed design asserted:
1. **The "vanishingly narrow" lost-update window is not narrow.** Six concurrent writers → **only two of six registrations survived**. Replaced with a lock whose holder pid is checked for liveness before it can be broken; 6/6 now survive. This is a deviation from design-v7.md §3b step 4 and has NOT been through the six rounds.
2. A cap-binding note consumed its once-per-session marker and then discarded its text whenever a real warning coincided, so it would never have been seen.

Also measured: bare `node` startup is **485 ms per hook invocation on this machine**; the hook's own work was 224 ms of that (per-row `path.resolve` over the log) and is now ~40 ms.

### Code review — two full rounds, 14 defects, 9 fixed and 5 still open
**Round 1 (both passes, all 9 fixed).**
- **Pass A** (Erez's `/code-review`, 6): null `lastFile` crash swallowing a whole warning; cap-note comparing against all live sessions including other projects; two containment roots ANDed; `MultiEdit` missing from the trigger set though the log records it; ignored `readSync` return value; an unreachable pid branch misreporting the failure.
- **Pass B** (independent, cold, opus — 3 material, all in the post-design lock/write path it correctly identified as least-reviewed): an unreadable session file treated as **proof of absence**, so pruning deleted a live session's registrations; **every** dropped-registration path completely silent, leaving the three-week review unable to tell "no collisions" from "nothing ever registered"; and a stale-lock breaker that broke on age alone, letting a stalled holder's live lock be stolen and its release then unlink the new holder's lock. Plus six adopted advisories.

**Round 2 Pass A (5, ALL STILL OPEN — full text in `notes/gen615-gen620-design/STATUS-resume-here.md`):** an unreadable edit log silently disabling the folder half with no note and no log line (no note key exists for the condition at all); a transient Windows sharing violation on the presence map — caused by the hook's own `renameSync` in another session — misreported as permanent corruption needing hand repair, unthrottled, with that prompt's registration skipped; a lock leaked when the holder-pid write fails, jamming every writer for the full 5 s age fallback despite a comment claiming immediate release; the `readFailures` guard's justification contradicted by measurement (all 8 live session records were written once at startup, one untouched 24 h into a live session — so registry `cwd` is frozen at startup and the folder half's containment gate silently covers the wrong tree if a session changes directory); and a case-sensitive file-count dedupe inflating the warning.

Round 2 Pass B was **not** run — it comes after these fixes.

**Pattern worth carrying:** 3 of round 2's 5 findings were again in the post-design lock/write path (filed as GEN-630), and one was the **same class** as round 1's "every dropped path is silent" reached by a different route — the first fix had addressed the instances named rather than the class (filed as GEN-631).

### Status
- **Done + verified:** design converged (six rounds); implementation written; 50/50 tests pass including concurrency, both cap cases, the sub-agent case and seven regression cases; `node --check` clean; two code-review rounds run.
- **Still open:** nothing is installed. `/vet-code` is paused mid-Step-3: fix the five round-2 findings, then re-run Pass B, then judge whether both passes must run a third time (Pass A needs Erez — `/code-review` is `disable-model-invocation`). Then the `/check` on the three build deviations, the Step-1b vetting record, the Step-4 pass-consumption assertion, phase B's two-session cases, mint, apply, verify.
- **Deliberately not done:** GEN-621/GEN-152 (another live session owned them). The five round-2 findings were **not** filed as tickets — they are the in-flight work of two In Progress tickets and are captured in full in the resume note; filing them separately would fragment the work.
- **Dead ends not worth retrying:** `list_sessions` for this purpose (wrong id space, unreachable from a hook); mtimes or git for folder presence (neither carries *which session* wrote, which is the whole point); any fixed time window anywhere in this mechanism.

### Two unknowns that could not be settled from stored artifacts
Whether a **resumed session keeps its `sessionId`** (if not, a long-running session's registration is pruned on resume and never re-created — GEN-615's own incident, silently), and whether **every session `kind` writes a registry file** (all 8 live records read `kind: "interactive"`, which is itself evidence other kinds exist). Both are assigned to build-time checks in design-v7.md §6, and phase B has a resume case.

### Concurrency observed live, in this project folder
Three other sessions were active in `Improve AI Infra` during this one (`36f12be8` wrapped GEN-576/600, `f00041c7` worked GEN-508 piece 1, `13a207fe` earlier). `f00041c7` had uncommitted work in `notes/gen508-piece1/` throughout — which is why this wrap staged files explicitly rather than by directory. A live demonstration of what GEN-615/620 are for.

### Follow-ups
- **Erez:** nothing. Next session starts from `notes/gen615-gen620-design/STATUS-resume-here.md` and fixes the five open findings; he is only needed again if a third `/code-review` round proves necessary.
- **Claude, at install:** the `settings.json` matcher must read `Read|Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit` — copying the sibling `inject-edit-refs.js` entry verbatim makes the MultiEdit fix inert. Register both events. Apply single-line via `update-config.ps1` (two targets, so two passes).
- **Claude, at install:** file the noise-review ticket with a three-week self-trigger carrying **both** bars and the calibration caveat (GEN-620's figures came from a 30-minute window; the shipped design uses a liveness bound, so a modestly higher early rate is expected).

Unresolved items filed: GEN-629, GEN-630, GEN-631.
Dropped learnings: none. Reversals judged non-learning: none.

Resume point and full flow state: `notes/gen615-gen620-design/STATUS-resume-here.md`.

## 2026-08-02 (7) — GEN-508 piece 1 designed, built to a working copy and reviewed twice; stopped for a scoping rebuild after two real payload shapes defeated it; nothing installed
<!-- session:8cbc4fb1-b0c2-4841-9721-793b077e1c43 -->

**What this session was.** Erez asked why GEN-508 was In Progress, then said "build". Scoped the work into three pieces and built piece 1: the Notion half of the ticket-quality gate — a fourth `enforceTicketVetting` arm in `auto-approve.js` plus a new `/vet-ticket` skill.

**Design (`/check`, converged in 3 rounds).** Seven material findings, all fixed. The load-bearing ones: the converged spec's claim that a PreToolUse hook cannot gate a Notion CREATE is false (it reasoned by analogy to new-FILE creation; a create names its parent data source in its own payload, and `notion-schema-guard.js` has gated creates in production since GEN-375) — so creates are gated BEFORE the write and Option 1 review-after is dropped; `notion-duplicate-page` and `notion-move-pages` are additional create paths the spec missed; move-OUT is in scope because de-listing a row drops every database property; substance became a deny-list so a renamed property fails closed; the "per-case waive" as originally written was inverted (declining a mint reinforces the block, it does not waive it), so a real waive lane was built; and the evidence check did not require a PASS verdict.

**Erez's decisions this session.** Accept the extra prompts at `/wrap` rather than exempt it (silent filing is what produced the near-duplicate incidents in GEN-508 §8). Approve a **summary card, not the body** — title, gist, parent, cross-referenced IDs, properties, reviewer verdict, with "show me the body" available. Several filings shown **together as one card list, approved in one action** (hence a batch pass; one approval must mean one dialog). A reviewer note must be **resolved** — amended or dismissed with a stated reason — before a ticket can file.

**Build + review.** Working copy built (342 lines, purely additive, `node --check` clean). Two full rounds of both code-review passes. Round 1: 10 findings (in-session) + 4 (independent). Round 2: 8 + 5. Round 2's independent pass found two silent bypasses verified against this machine's own captured payloads: a real `notion-create-pages` call nests `parent` inside `pages[0]` with no top-level `parent`, and a real `notion-update-page` call arrives as `{"data":"<whole payload as a string>"}`. Root cause: the scoping layer was written against the published tool schema, not against captured traffic. Also verified and corrected mid-flow: this machine runs `defaultMode: "auto"`, so a gate that defers on a Notion write is silently approved — every `return []` is an approval, not a prompt.

**Stopped, per the fix-on-fix rule.** Two rounds each produced a fresh fail-open of the same class. Erez chose to rebuild the "is this a ticket?" layer so payload shape cannot matter (normalise, then search the whole payload for a Team-Tasks marker) rather than patch the five open findings — and to do it in a new session.

**Handoff.** A "BUILD STATE 2026-08-02" section was written to the top of GEN-508 and verified live via REST (heading present, priority-exception callout and original spec intact, properties untouched). Artifacts moved out of the session scratchpad into `notes/gen508-piece1/` — working copy, diff, skill draft, converged design, README.

**Also settled:** `/code-review` exists but is user-invocation-only, so Claude cannot launch it; both rounds required Erez to type it. Two standing rules must be amended as part of this build (the `/wrap` silent-filing rule, and the drafting rule's "body" requirement vs card approval).

**The central finding, and the reason the run was stopped.** The vetting flow pins a content hash at stage 1 and relies on it through every later stage without re-checking. **Verification that was real.** A pass-consumption assertion built in an isolated fake `.claude` tree (hardlinked hook, so its own path resolution pointed at the fixture): blocked without a pass, approved-and-consumed with one, and refused on reuse — 3/3. The contract fixture ran 19/19, against the copy current at the time.

**Four corrections to Erez, each from live state rather than pushback.** I reported the caller-doc rewrite as awaiting his approval when both files already carried it. I said five vetting records existed with four stale; there were four, of which two were safe to delete — the reviewer caught that my wording would have swept in GEN-218's record, whose hash is this install's rollback baseline. I called GEN-218 a completed ticket; it is Review at Highest. <!-- session:72bd489c-e456-4b2d-be01-ab88e5e4034b -->

**Started as a one-line question** ("what model effort level do you need to continue GEN-443? verify") and became the whole of GEN-443's remaining work bar the final write.

Both files verified byte-identical to the vetted text by sha256; both passes consumed.

**Step 3 taken to the edge of install, then deliberately stopped.** Built script, fixture and gate assertions are all green; the live `prepend-log.ps1` is UNTOUCHED. Full cold-pickup state is on GEN-443's "STATE AS OF 2026-08-02 (2) — START HERE" block.

**Five code-review rounds, and rounds 2 and 3 each found a defect introduced by the previous round's fix.** This is the substance of the session:
- *Round 1:* blind pass PASS; my own pass found 10, fixed 6 (ordinal comparison, millisecond recovery-file stamps, three false comments, two fixture accept-cases).
- *Round 2 (REVISE, 2 material):* the guard exited on the FIRST violation while both callers permit exactly ONE retry — so any entry breaking two rules was a deterministic blocked wrap. And the recovery file's own text told its reader to hand-append content that is by construction still malformed, which would plant the very corruption the guard prevents. My round-1 timestamp fix had also made the orphan-file problem strictly worse. Fixed: accumulate all violations into one message; CAUTION wording keyed off the violation type.
- *Round 3 (REVISE, 1 material, caused by the round-2 fix):* the four checks are not independent — the body-heading scan presupposes the first-line check passed. With both reporting, a leading-blank entry (the commonest violation) was told to fix its heading AND to demote that same heading. Reproduced by running it. This hit my stated stop-and-re-examine bar.
- *The re-examination overturned my own recommendation.* I formed a proposal to revert and ship, ran it through `/check` first, and both lenses rejected it: reverting would widen the deterministic-failure surface from one input pair to six, my "rare" premise had no evidence (and the repo's own data contradicted it), and the revert would silently re-open round 2's second finding because the CAUTION text is triggered from inside the block being deleted. The converged answer was smaller than either option I had put up: merge the two heading rules into ONE scan branching on count and position.
- *Rounds 4 and 5:* both blind passes PASS, each re-deriving from scratch that all twenty combinations of heading state and TOC state are correctable within the one retry allowed. My round-4 pass found 9 (4 fixed: stale line numbers in the combined case, a retry-policy restatement inside the script, a comment claiming unchanged predicate bodies, a header listing three of four rules). My round-5 pass found 9, all advisory.

**Evidence, measured rather than asserted.** Contract fixture 19/19 against the build. The SAME fixture scores 10/14 FAIL against the currently-installed script, with all seven contract cases accepted and written — so the suite discriminates, and the corruption is live in production today. Also measured on the installed script: bad arguments return 1 where 2 is documented, a malformed entry burns the full ~180s lock budget before failing, and lone-CR input misplaces the session marker by two lines. Gate-consumption assertion 4/4 in a throwaway fixture tree: with a pass the write is approved and the pass renamed, without one it is blocked at exit 2, a single-line shell write consumes, and the multi-line form defers leaving the pass live. Rule frequency measured across 58 real appender-written entries in all three projects: displaced heading 3.4%, extra body heading 5.2%, both together 1.7% — that measurement is what decided the last fix was worth making.

**Why the install was deferred, and it is a real finding not an excuse.** `/vet-code` Step 7 directs a full-file Write for a non-locked script. The vetted file is 650 lines; re-emitting it exactly at the end of a very long session risks consuming the one-time pass and stranding a protected file half-written (the GEN-587 incident, on a much smaller edit). A single-line byte write would be exact by construction and does consume the pass — proven in the fixture tree — but Step 7 forbids the shell path. Rather than deviate unilaterally on the irreversible step, the write goes to a fresh session. Evidence appended to GEN-600, which already owns that open question.

**Backup taken before anything:** `~/.claude-staging/gen443-backup/prepend-log.ps1.pre-gen443-20260802-160444`, byte-identical, and matching the baseline hash recorded at session start — so the live script had not drifted.

**GEN-58 (reasoning-failure log), Vol. 6:** a NEW failure class **T** — *each component verified against its own spec, the interaction never verified* — from the guard-vs-retry-budget defect that a design panel, a blind pass and my own ten-angle review all missed while each artifact was individually correct. Added a supported, append-only way to retire a known-benign unpaired `detect` in `~/.claude/hooks/signal-surface-pending.jsonl`, so a confirmed false alarm stops re-surfacing at every `/wrap`.

- **Chose option 1 of the three the ticket listed: a distinct `kind:"ack"` line.** Applied to `/wrap` Step 3b in `~/.claude/skills/wrap/SKILL.md` through `/vet-rule` — converged `/check` panel, 2 rounds, 6 independent `check-reviewer` agents.

- **Review found a real defect in my first draft:** the reconcile keyed on `session`+`prompt`, but the detector appends one `detect` per qualifying tool call, so acking one file's orphan would have silently and permanently retired a sibling orphan nobody had reviewed — the exact loss the log exists to prevent. ## 2026-08-02 (4) — GEN-557 shipped end-to-end: six review rounds, a 593x regression caught, fence-masking built then dropped
<!-- session:ceffe322-f532-48c2-8269-36bb80a3b590 -->

**Resumed GEN-557 from the 2026-07-30 pause and shipped it.** The session opened on "what effort level is needed to resume GEN-557? verify" — answered xhigh/Opus 5 from `notes/effort-model-reference.md` plus the ticket's own remaining work, then ran the whole remaining gate.

**The rig had to be rebuilt.** The 07-30 session banked only the README, so every measuring script was gone. Rebuilt from the README's inlined source, and **banked the scripts this time** at `notes/gen557-selfaudit-measurement/rig/` (24 files, git-tracked) so it cannot happen a third time. The corpus is smaller than 07-30's — **4,356 turn-final messages from 157 transcripts, vs 4,580/170** — because Claude Code prunes old transcripts. Re-baselined rather than comparing; production baseline came out at exactly 77 either way.

**The three open design findings, all resolved by measurement rather than judgement.** (1) The dominant pattern `nothing to (correct|fix)` had been validated on 4 of ~120 hits; read **all 125** reachable unquoted instances — 125/125 were the target class, 0 false, so it needs neither position-anchoring nor a `needsClean` gate (both were measured unnecessary, not skipped). (2) Ticket shape (a), the "done, verified" roll-call, had no coverage; the panel's suggested one-bullet-line anchor was built and **rejected** — it fired on a legitimate "where things stand" report (corpus t2553, `- **GEN-550 — shipped, verified, Done.**`). Requiring **two** such bulleted lines within 400 chars fires on exactly 1 of 2,585 reachable turns: the recurrence itself. (3) The quote guard's false-negative direction was measured — it silences 4 turns, all 4 genuine quoted references, 0 genuine hits wrongly suppressed.

**Design panel converged in 2 rounds** (pre-mortem/holistic/soundness, then a holistic re-review): round 1 caught that finding (3) was only half-closed — the panel's bar required either narrowing the guard's scope *or* Erez's explicit sign-off to widen it, and neither had been done. **Focus:** Erez asked whether any rule/mechanism/open ticket was meant to fix the recurring "you have to ask if a drafted ticket has all needed context" problem, then had me design the fix (an enlarged GEN-508) to a build-ready spec.

- The behavioral completeness-bar rule already exists in global CLAUDE.md ("draft the full proposal … stand on its own"); GEN-491 (Done) captured the recurring problem; [GEN-508](https://app.notion.com/p/3a36e495d07c81fb9a55ddc315639c7f) (Backlog) already proposed the hard-gate mechanism, parked with "build only if the behavioral rule proves insufficient." Erez still having to ask *is* that trigger.

**Design (converged through two full /suggest + /check panel rounds, all three lenses each round):**
- Enlarged GEN-508 from "structural completeness gate on creation" to **"Enforce all ticket-quality rules on every Notion + Jira create/edit via an independent-review gate"** (title updated to match).
- Erez's settled decisions: judge-before-filing (fix silently or consult); airtight guarantee with a per-case waive; consults by urgency; both trackers, create+edit together; review only writes that matter (every create + body/priority-field edits, skip housekeeping — a hook-drawn line); an **independent** reviewer (Claude can't self-certify — Erez pointed at how /check works); create-side = Option 1 (allow create, review-immediately-after) since a hook can't gate a create.
- Architecture: a `/vet-ticket` skill + `enforceTicketVetting` hook arm, a **direct sibling of the existing staging/vetting/check gate family** in auto-approve.js (verified live: enforceStaging 626, enforceVetting 940, VETTING_PASS_DIR 707, target+field-not-hash binding 547; createJiraIssue confirmed ungated).
- Honest limits recorded on the ticket: create-side is behavioral not airtight; the pass proves a review ran, not that it was competent; mechanical floor is independent of self-report not of inputs.

**Actions taken:**
- Rewrote GEN-508 body (full converged 8-section spec) + title; verified via REST (40 blocks, all sections, old body gone).
- GEN-58: logged a Class D recurrence trace (two create-side mis-reasonings — assumed creates could be hard-gated; mis-costed Option 1 as one write) on Vol. 5; bumped Class D count 89x→90x. Both verified via REST.
- Captured the converged spec to a scratch file for cold-start, then (per Erez) moved it into GEN-508's body and deleted the scratch file.

## 2026-07-23 (3)
<!-- session:975eedc7-d9bd-48bf-b81e-7d2b10bac9fb -->

**Focus:** GEN-467 (duplicate/narrated "For you" block) — root-cause investigation, four design iterations, and a scoped handoff for the structural fix (deferred to a future session per Erez).

**What happened.** Erez pasted a verification-walkthrough block Claude had emitted ("...filed, verified ✓ closed... Nothing to correct") and objected that these process-narration messages "drive him nuts" — the claim-linter was meant to catch unverified claims silently, not narrate its checking. Investigated: the narration issue is what GEN-507 (Done) was built to suppress; today's leak is a coverage gap in that detector → filed **GEN-557** (widen the self-audit detector to catch enumerated "done, verified ✓ / nothing to correct" walkthroughs), Backlog, with verbatim trigger text + counter-example + vetting-lock note.

Then Claude emitted **two "For you" blocks back-to-back** (a block on a reply, then a second bare-correction block on the continuation). Erez asked which ticket had been meant to fix this and why it didn't. Found **GEN-467** (Bug, was Review). Its block-after-check convention (2026-07-19) handles corrections folded into a not-yet-sent block, but has only instruction-text (no structural guard) for a correction arriving AFTER the block already went out — today's exact case. GEN-467 reopened Review → **In Progress** and its pre-agreed escalation pursued.

**Four design iterations (all via /check panels, all rejected → converged understanding):**
1. v1 (marker-keyed instruction clause) — rejected: not structural, and already present verbatim in the shipped file (a no-op); trigger mis-reasoned (block rides the stop_hook_active continuation).
2. v2 (loop-and-hold blocking hook, cap 3) — escalated: depends on 3 unverified harness behaviors (prompt_id stability across forced re-run; whether a hook can re-block while stop_hook_active; cross-hook stacking on intermediate passes). One reviewer wrongly claimed streaming defeats the un-narrated goal; a parallel reviewer DISPROVED it with a verbatim doc quote (decision:"block" "Blocks the response from being shown").
3. v3 (/check-style orchestration loop, Erez's pointer) — settles all 3 v2 questions by making them moot (loop lives in the model's own turn orchestration, not fragile hook re-entry), but trades away structural invisibility (compliance-dependent).
4. v4 (tighten existing note text) — rejected: the note ALREADY says the target behavior; the gap is ACTIVATION, not wording (same conclusion as GEN-507). More instruction text on a channel already not-followed can't deliver "reliably."

**Key realization (Erez's):** the check already happens pre-block (claim-linter's additionalContext lands at the start of the continuation, before the block is composed — GEN-450 Phase-0/0b record). So it was never a timing problem; the defect is composition-discipline (activation) on the continuation.

**Core learning:** every prose/instruction fix is the same compliance-dependent fix-class that has failed every time on this behavior. Reliability can only come from a STRUCTURAL mechanism (hook enforces, not instructs). Told this, Erez chose to pursue the structural route in a FUTURE session, and had this whole exploration logged into GEN-467 as a cold-pickup handoff (goal, all attempts + rejections, verified platform facts, the required empirical probe of the 3 behaviors, design constraints). GEN-467 kept at **In Progress**, Priority **High** (Erez's explicit call, overriding a re-derivation toward To-Do/Medium).

**Decisions/tickets:**
- GEN-557 filed (widen self-audit detector) — Backlog, Medium, unassigned.
- GEN-467 reopened → In Progress; full cold-pickup handoff appended + verified live via REST (97 blocks, 7 sections). Structural route deferred to a future session; probe-first required.
- GEN-58: two Class-D recurrence traces logged (v1 no-op designed without diffing shipped code; near-relay of an unverified reviewer inference) → Vol. 5; Class D count 87→89.

Unresolved items filed: GEN-558 (distinguish real vs manufactured decisions; act instead of asking — filed with an open classification question re: overlap with GEN-507).

## 2026-07-23 — GEN-462: break-glass reaper (kernel-free) shipped
<!-- session:51e49b74-c9a4-43aa-95d4-753cf59576dc -->

**Shipped (GEN-462 → Done).** Built and installed a new SessionStart hook, `sessionstart-configunlock-reaper.js`, that makes the `.config-unlock` break-glass unable to *silently* persist across sessions. At each session start it reaps any `.config-unlock` sentinel not backed by a valid unexpired token in `~/.claude-staging/config-unlock-passes/`, staying **silent on success** (legitimate open, or self-healed reap) and surfacing a loud alarm **only** when an unaccountable sentinel can't be deleted. The security kernel `configUnlocked()` was left byte-for-byte unchanged (verified). Trust anchor is *location* (token in the prompt-forced `~/.claude-staging` sibling), not crypto.

**Design journey (long, several reversals — see learnings).** Went through many `/check` rounds: v1 surfacer → v2 kernel-free expiry → v3 age-only (rejected: false-certainty) → v4 provenance record (rejected: forgeable + not atomic) → "option 2" unforgeable/kernel-editing (Erez chose it, then the panel + Claude found the malicious-forger threat doesn't apply to a single-user local tool) → **final kernel-free location-anchored reaper**. Erez then set the operating principle: *"you handle things on your own; when successful, silence; when there's a problem, involve me"* — which resolved the last open design question (no routine "gate open" note).

**Build (via `/vet-code`):** design `/check` converged; two independent code-review passes (cold sub-agent PASS + high-effort in-session pass) — both advisories folded in (fail-toward-showing outer catch; `process.exitCode` flush idiom); live-verify 23/23 across 8 scenarios (absent / valid-token-preserved / expired / no-token / empty-dir / bad-json / numeric-expires / undeletable-alarm); regression: 3 existing SessionStart hooks untouched. Not a background-launch change → no antivirus arming. Two vetting passes minted (hook file + settings.json registration), Erez-approved; applied; install verified byte-identical; kernel confirmed unchanged.

**Notion:**
- GEN-462 → Done (verified via REST).
- Filed GEN-552 (Urgent · Highest 🔥) — legitimate flows must write the reaper's accountability token so a real break-glass survives a session boundary; GEN-553 (Not-urgent · High) — add the reaper hook to `sync.ps1` backup set (surfaced by a BACKUP-COVERAGE warning on install). ## 2026-07-21 (2) — GEN-520 design (planning only; nothing built) + handoff
<!-- session:e5b95d3b-820b-4a46-ae80-c1f837d578db -->

**Task:** "Suggest a plan for GEN-520," then design it to a buildable state.

**Outcome:** No code or rule was built or changed this session. The session produced a settled design and a clean handoff on the ticket, plus two reasoning-failure log entries. The only external writes were to GEN-520's own properties/body, the new GEN-529 ticket, and GEN-58.

**What GEN-520 turned out to be (goal corrected 3× via Erez's steers):** Not "ensure the three priority fields get set on update." The real goal: **when Claude materially edits a Team-Tasks ticket's *content* via a tool call, re-derive Importance/Gain from the new content and recompute Priority.** Scope = Claude's tool-call edits to Team-Tasks tickets only; out of scope = Erez's manual Notion edits, ticket creation, property-only-edit triggers, and any after-the-fact sweep.

**Design journey (recorded so it isn't re-walked):**
- Rejected: create-time gate (wrong problem); session-end/periodic consistency sweep (can't scope to "changes only Claude does"); PreToolUse hook variants with a deny→re-issue loop-break (per-session marker over-suppressed later edits; 60s-TTL had window races; content-hash broke on non-byte-identical retries); `updatedInput` (silent / can't compute the value).
- **Decisive fatal-flaw finding (max-effort /check panel, reading the actual code):** a PreToolUse soft `deny` does NOT override the settings allow-list that pre-approves `notion-update-page` (documented in `auto-approve.js` from GEN-103/281/337). So every `deny`-based hook design would have silently never fired. The allow-list-overriding pre-write channels are `ask` (prompts Erez — wrong audience) and `exit(2)` (reason-delivery-to-Claude unverified).
- **Decision (Erez approved): Option 1 — a rule, not a hook.** Add one clause to the global "Before creating or materially changing a ticket in a tracker" rule making a material *content* edit a trigger to re-derive Importance/Gain (the "recompute Priority whenever either input changes" step already exists in that rule). A rule fires in Claude's own reasoning at edit time, needs no machinery, and covers edit paths a hook can't see (raw REST `PATCH /v1/blocks/{id}`).

**Verified platform facts (WebFetch of code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks + live REST this session):** PreToolUse `deny`/`ask` block pre-exec and `deny` shows Claude the reason; `additionalContext` is delivered after the tool result; `ask` escalates to an Erez dialog; 600s command-hook timeout; `GET /v1/pages/{id}` under `Notion-Version: 2022-06-28` returns `parent.database_id` (Team-Tasks REST db id `fe198002-6618-48d7-ae04-56f8cee479f3`).

**GEN-520 handoff state:** title changed to "Re-evaluate a Team-Tasks ticket's priority when Claude edits its content"; Status = To Do (unassigned); body fully rewritten (goal, decision + why, ruled-out list, open threads, references) and verified byte-exact via REST. Next action for a future session: draft the one-clause rule via the `/vet-rule` flow (recommended: Opus 4.8, high effort).

**Reasoning-failure log (GEN-58):** logged a Class-E recurrence (fix-on-fix / solution-anchoring: anchored on "a hook" and re-fixed it across shifting goals instead of re-deriving from the goal; header bumped 18x→19x, +1 recurrence trace). The session also exhibited Class-A/D (asserting platform capabilities/exhaustiveness later shown wrong) — captured as the GEN-529 enforceable candidate rather than a separate GEN-58 element.

## 2026-07-21 (1) — **Effort-tag enforcement shipped into `stop-foryou-nudge.js` via full `/vet-code`; fixes both effort-estimation failure modes Erez raised (missing tags + ungrounded numbers). Opus 4.8, xhigh. Entirely AI-infra work.**
<!-- session:68b30c17-6c2f-485c-96ab-c5b523b07b60 -->

Erez: across multiple sessions my effort estimations were "unfounded" and sometimes "not given at all" — tackle it; he thought GEN-466 covered it, maybe partially. Confirmed GEN-466 was a *different* problem (an automatic hook to NUDGE an effort *change* mid-work, dropped as not viable — a `UserPromptSubmit`/`PreToolUse` hook can't read the live effort value). The actual complaint is that the **effort-tagging rule** (global CLAUDE.md, "When a 📌 For you block puts a decision…") is self-policed with no enforcement, so tags go missing (Failure 1) and, when present, are fabricated rather than looked up from `notes/effort-model-reference.md` (Failure 2). Erez picked "option 2": keep the tag terse/bare, fix reliability + grounding; hard constraints — don't grow the global CLAUDE.md, output stays bare.

**Key discovery that reshaped the design:** the existing `stop-foryou-nudge.js` Stop hook already inspects `last_assistant_message` end-of-turn and injects `additionalContext` — the enforcement layer GEN-466 thought impossible (it tested the wrong hook type). Also verified from `gen450-stop-probe.jsonl` that the Stop stdin carries a live `effort.level` (33/33 payloads) — but the converged design does NOT use it (see below).

**Design converged via 3-round independent `/check` panel (11 reviewer passes).** The panel found a material flaw in EVERY version, including two of my own fixes: (a) a naive Failure-1 detector would be a silent **no-op** — the block+tag rides the *continuation* turn, which every Stop hook skips via `stop_hook_active` (the GEN-467 duplicate-block guard); (b) my "compare tagged-effort vs actual `effort.level`" idea was **inverted** — divergence is the NORMAL signature of a valid level-change recommendation, so it would fire on correct tags and miss fabricated ones; (c) my sentinel "fix" for (a) reintroduced the GEN-467 bug AND was unnecessary. Reviewer-authored final design (I contributed no surviving load-bearing idea — the whole session is a Class-D "designed on an unverified primitive" instance, the exact pattern that sank this feature before):

**What shipped:** extended the always-loaded global `CLAUDE.md` ticket-drafting rule ("Before creating or materially changing a ticket in a tracker, draft the full proposal…") with a completeness bar: the drafted body must stand on its own — problem+why, background to act (paths/IDs/links/prior decisions), next action or acceptance criteria, who verifies it where relevant — re-read against that bar before presenting; scaled to complexity; with an inline "not 'unrequested info'" guard and a descriptive carve-out for the reasoning-failure log-writes exception. Applied via `update-global-rule.ps1` through the `/vet-rule` flow (check-record + minted check pass), exit 0, verified live and synced to Drive.

**How it got there (the reasoning arc worth keeping):**
1. First proposal — put the bar in the `notion-howto` skill — was **killed by the /check panel**: all three reviewers + this repo's own HISTORY (2026-07-01) confirmed skills do NOT auto-load, so a skill-homed rule fires only when explicitly invoked = the exact unreliability being fixed. Claude had asserted "notion-howto already loads at that moment" from the skill's description without verifying — a verify-before-asserting miss Erez's rule already covers.
2. Reframed to a resident rule; Erez's question "don't we already have a rule?" surfaced that the fix belonged folded into the existing line-59 rule (not a new standalone rule), since line 59 already fires at draft time and governs the body.
3. Contradiction check (prompted by Erez) caught a real conflict: the bar, nested in line 59, could be read as NOT covered by the GEN-58 immediate-log exception (line 185) → would force immediate reasoning-failure logs to satisfy a stand-alone bar. Fixed with an explicit carve-out.
4. Minimality pass (prompted by Erez "is this the shortest?") trimmed a full hedge sentence to a ~5-word inline tag; split reviewer verdict resolved on the shared cheap fix.
5. Final vet-rule confirming pass caught that the carve-out hardcoded "GEN-58" (a ticket number) into an always-loaded file — a line-155 violation — fixed by referencing the exception descriptively instead.
6. Confirmed (Erez's questions) the mechanical/behavioral split: behavioral ticket rules stay always-loaded; Notion tool *gotchas* already live in the hook-injected `hooks/refs/notion.md`, not the skill. Nothing moved.

**Follow-up filed:** GEN-508 — "Add a structural ticket-creation gate enforcing the completeness bar" (GEN-86, Backlog, task, unassigned): optional hard-gate hardening of the behavioral rule, build only if the rule proves insufficient over the next several tickets.

## 2026-07-20 (5) — Silence-on-success self-audit narration ban (global CLAUDE.md)
<!-- session:1479d958-a207-433e-97e5-66e7f895b6c1 -->

**Trigger.** Erez asked why, in another session ("Opus 4.8 effort for gen 501"), a reply ended with a self-audit line: "…no unverified assertions. No state was changed. No block is owed." — and to verify it.

**Investigation.** Located and re-read that session's transcript (via session-mgmt tools). Verdict: the three claims in that line were factually true and read-only, but writing the line at all was a mistake — that turn was a pure Q&A owing no "📌 For you" block, so under "Default to silence on success" it owed silence, not a narrated self-audit. Correctly concluding "no block is owed" means emitting nothing, not a sentence saying so.

**Prior coverage.** Searched under GEN-86: the issue lineage already exists — GEN-151 (original report of an unneeded process note, merged), GEN-314 ("Stop surfacing for-me-only content", Done — added the governing rule). The rule existed; the failure was non-application, plus a narrow gap (a clean/null verdict reading as a "conclusion" rather than "the checking").

**Decision & fix.** Erez chose to fix via a rule edit (not a hook), broad "Scope 2" (never emit any commentary about internal process on a silence-owed turn). Formed the edit via /suggest; ran /check to convergence — 3 rounds, 4 lenses (pre-mortem, holistic, soundness, rule-check; final round on Opus). R1: all REVISE (edit anchored to narrow verification clause; false premise that the opening sentence didn't already cover it; over-fit enumeration). R2: soundness+pre-mortem PASS, holistic+rule-check REVISE (closed list still echoed the incident phrase; NEW conflict — absolute "never as a free-standing note" contradicted the unchanged "a claim you must flag as unverified" carve-out; clarity risk). R3: both PASS — incident echo dropped, true catch-all, conflict fixed via "never overrides the exception stream below or a report a standing rule requires inside the block", reasoning-as-content carve-out added.

**Applied** via /vet-rule gate: wrote check-record (referencing real R3 reviewer transcripts), minted single-use check pass (Erez approved), applied through update-global-rule.ps1 (exit 0, synced to Drive), verified installed file hash matches approved working copy byte-for-byte. The edit adds a clause to the "Default to silence on success" rule (global CLAUDE.md line 73).

**Advisory carried forward.** Reviewers judged the root cause was likely non-application of an already-covering rule, so text alone may not fully prevent recurrence; Erez knowingly chose rule-over-hook. Enforcement is the deferred lever → filed GEN-507 with a re-evaluate bar (build only if the failure recurs).

**Tickets:** GEN-507 created (enforcement follow-up, Backlog, unassigned, under GEN-86).

## 2026-07-20 (5): GEN-503 shipped — vetting-gate fail-open fixed via /vet-code; wider settings.json blast radius found; GEN-504/505/506 filed
<!-- session:ae834e73-22a8-42a8-9840-dc3e51c8e746 -->

**GEN-503 — vetting-gate fail-open (Done).** Fixed the fail-open in `auto-approve.js`'s vetting gate: `resolveUpdateConfigFile`'s `-File` extraction regex `/-File\s+.../i` was unanchored, so for `-Op write-file -File auto-approve.js` it matched the `-file` TAIL of the token `write-file`, captured the next token `-File` as the "filename", the `$ManagedFiles` lookup failed → null → no vetting target → gate deferred (fail-open). Net effect: EVERY `-Op write-file` update-config.ps1 call bypassed the vetting-pass requirement. Fix = prepend a non-capturing leading boundary `(?:^|\s)` to the flag match in `resolveUpdateConfigFile` (`-File`) and `ucArg` (`-Op`/`-ContentFile`). Two functional lines; the rest comments (incl. tightening three misleading "fails safe → prompt" comments). Installed byte-identical (normalized sha256 `9e66b18d…50eda2`).

**Wider blast radius than the ticket documented:** because the buggy resolve returned null for every write-file, the global `settings.json` **hooks-registration arm** (`settingsHooksChanged` via `k === GLOBAL_SETTINGS_KEY`) was ALSO failing open for write-file edits — not just hook/script `.js`/`.ps1` writes. The fix restores that arm too. Surfaced by the /check pre-mortem reviewer.

**Full /vet-code flow run:** Step 0 gate self-check passed (enforceVetting/findVettingPassFile intact; ran on Opus 4.8, top tier). Step 1 /check converged in 1 round — fix mechanism unanimously PASS across 3 Opus reviewers (pre-mortem/holistic/soundness); the sole REVISE was fixture-coverage (over-block regression + settings.json hooks-arm), folded in. Steps 3 code-review: Pass A (in-session /code-review high) no material findings; Pass B (independent check-reviewer, Opus) PASS. `node --check` clean. Step 4 live-verify: built `gen503-verify.js`, a real spawnSync integration fixture in a fake .claude tree — **6/12 FAIL on the unmodified live file (proves it discriminates the bug), 12/12 PASS on the fixed hook**, including approve-and-consume and the settings.json hooks-arm. Not a background-launch change → Step 4a/8a skipped. Manual GEN-498-style pre-apply baseline re-diff done (raw hash `F19CFFE7…AC035` unchanged) — no concurrent edit. Minted pass (Erez-approved write), applied via `update-config.ps1 -Op write-file`, verified installed byte-identical. Confirmed live: the installed hook now hard-blocks a chained hook-write and gates `-Op write-file`.

**Observed the bug one last time in the act:** the minted pass was NOT consumed at apply time — the still-live buggy hook fell open and routed the apply through the ordinary permission layer instead of the consume path. Install was safe (vetted, approved, hash-verified); inert pass deleted. Kept the `gen503-record.json` vetting-record for audit.

**Not bundled with GEN-498** (concurrent-baseline race in the apply procedure) — distinct defect, kept separate.

**Session learnings filed (capture-only, apply later needs /check + approval):**
- GEN-506 — /vet-code Step 4 should assert the vetting pass is CONSUMED on the sanctioned apply path (the general lesson behind this bug slipping past GEN-488's own vet).
- GEN-504 — consolidate the two update-config flag-value extractors into one tested parser (kills the bug class at one code path).
- GEN-505 — audit remaining `auto-approve.js` guard comments that overstate the "fails safe → prompt" guarantee.

Unresolved items filed: GEN-504, GEN-505, GEN-506
Dropped learnings: none

The documented remedy: write notes as declarative factual statements. The harness always wraps additionalContext in a system-reminder; the author controls only the payload text, so the lever is phrasing, not markup.

**Step 1 SHIPPED — both Stop-hook notes reworded to declarative background-state** (stop-claim-linter.js, stop-foryou-nudge.js). **Step 2 (logger to measure whether step 1 held) — REJECTED by /check and PARKED by Erez.** 2 Opus reviewers (holistic + pre-mortem) REVISE, converged: auto-detecting narration is worse than no instrument — step 1's own note text contains the scanner's trigger tokens ("a check ran","correction","verify","For you"), so it fires on legit corrections/echoes; and because surfacing is actionable-only, every false positive becomes a false "reframe failed -> revisit blocking hook" alarm pushing toward the shelved risky hook. **Option (c) surfaced by Erez's pushback and ruled out.** Erez asked whether a local folder on `C:` mirrored by Google Drive's desktop client ("Folders from your computer") shares (b)'s downsides. Verified (WebSearch + `/check`, 2 rounds): real (installed client v127 supports it) but NOT airtight — documented `.git` corruption from Drive writing into synced folders (desktop.ini injection), and **the client cannot exclude `.git`** (verified, no such feature); deletions propagate (mirror, not history; ~30-day trash); no secret gate; silent-pause risk. If a Drive copy is ever wanted, the safe route is Drive as an *additional destination of (b)* (push to an archive repo inside the synced folder), itself unproven against the corruption class → needs a live test. My presenting the choice as a closed (a)/(b) binary was the Class-C reasoning miss (see below).

**(b) stress-tested — all `/check`-converged (3 lenses, 2 rounds each):**
- Same-PC concurrency (4-5 sessions/day on one repo is current reality): collisions → retry → snapshot delayed minutes, never corrupts; files always safe on disk. Mitigations are TO-BE-BUILT (not true today): isolated-index snapshots + **per-session** ref naming (finer than per-machine — the soundness lens caught that per-machine alone still races same-PC sessions).
- Separate backup channel (refs outside `refs/heads/*`) keeps main history curated; those refs are invisible in GitHub's web UI but restorable ("not on GitHub.com" ≠ "not backed up").
- Hard rules the machinery must obey: reads+pushes only (no pull/rebase/checkout/reset); every snapshot pushed to a NAMED ref (dangling commits get GC'd ~14 days); detect + loudly flag a mid-merge repo rather than snapshot conflict debris.
- Multi-PC (future): per-machine + per-session ref namespacing; git refuses silent overwrite of diverged work (verified); Drive-mirror instead makes conflict-copies. Costs: per-PC one-script install; the catch-all repo needs per-machine labeling for "promote?" triage.
- Cursor/other tools = biggest limit of hook-only (b): a PostToolUse hook only fires on *Claude* writes. Fix = a **scheduled sweep** (Windows task ~15-30 min, tool-agnostic). Three sweep caveats each got a design answer to live-test at build: sleep gap → catch-up-on-wake + dead-man's-switch; torn mid-save files → settle-time (snapshot only files quiet ~1 min) + never overwrite older snapshots; scheduled-task GitHub credentials → live-test.
- Inherent git limits recorded: ignored files, quarantined secrets, >100 MB (future game/asset project → LFS), snapshot buildup (retention/compaction from day one), network (retried), single-account risk (Drive second target).

**Scope narrowed by Erez this session:** currently one device, Claude-only. Cursor-coverage and multi-device move to **two future tickets Erez already holds — he has not yet given the IDs; next session must ask** and copy the deferred sweep-for-other-tools + multi-PC analysis onto them.

Sweep-only = one task, single actor, no collision machinery, covers non-Claude changes in minutes, is the backbone the future tickets need; hook is addable later (an addition, not a redesign) if the ~15-30 min lag ever matters. Key distinction surfaced for Erez: next-session latency for non-Claude edits means *no backup exists at all* in that window — unlike the accepted transient-failure case (already backed up, only a push retry pending).

## 2026-07-09 (4) — GEN-382 renamed to "Make backup of everything we work on airtight" → In Progress; first design failed `/check`; pivot designed; decision handed off

Session on project 3 (Improve AI Infra), Opus 4.8. Erez asked to go over GEN-382 and return with guiding questions or a converged plan. **Nothing was built or applied** — this was investigation + design that ended on an open decision, fully handed off onto the ticket. The only mutations: GEN-382 (handoff section + status + rename) and two GEN-58 log writes.

**What GEN-382 was, and what it became.** Filed as "Backup Gap" — one hook file (`notion-fetch-staleness.js`) flagged as missing from `sync.ps1`'s backup set. Investigation found that file is *already* backed up in all three locations and already in `$FileMap` (sync.ps1:136) — **but Erez had added it manually** at a past `/wrap`. That manual fix IS the point: the existing coverage watchdog (`Test-BackupCoverage`, built under GEN-140, warn-only) is not airtight — it emits a warning nobody is forced to act on. Erez restated the real goal: **every file we create or change, across all current and future projects, backed up by a mechanism that can't be silently skipped** — not just config. Ticket renamed accordingly (verified via REST) and set → In Progress (primary ticket, substantive work).

**Also resolved the ticket's "covered elsewhere?" ask:** GEN-382 is essentially a duplicate of [GEN-140](https://app.notion.com/p/3746e495d07c81bab600ce35574d8498) (Done — built the coverage watchdog). GEN-382 now carries the broader airtight goal GEN-140 didn't.

**5 design decisions Erez locked (via one-at-a-time Q&A):** (1) scope = everything, config is just one category; (2) if a file isn't backed up, back it up automatically — no prompt/block — EXCEPT a suspected secret, which surfaces (fail-closed scan before anything leaves the machine); (3) transient push failure (network/GitHub/Drive down) never blocks — wrap completes, unmissable notice, next session retries; (4) enumeration = session-driven minus provably-throwaway (scratchpad/`%TEMP%`/transcripts, `node_modules`/build), uncertainty always resolves to backing up; (5) brand-new location → protect in a catch-all + flag "promote to its own repo?", never auto-create a named GitHub repo.

**The first design FAILED `/check` (3 reviewers — pre-mortem, holistic, soundness — all REVISE).** Design was "enumerate changed files at session end via the two edit logs, then back them up." Two premises were **verified false from source** (reviewers read the files):
- **Edit logs are incomplete** (`auto-approve.js`): `auto-approved-edits.jsonl` logs only Edit/Write/MultiEdit into project roots — not NotebookEdit, not shell-classified-safe writes (script output etc.), not moves/renames/deletes; `deferred-calls.jsonl` logs only unsafe/unrecognized calls. So log-based enumeration silently misses whole write classes — the exact failure this ticket exists to kill, moved one layer down.
- **There is no `SessionEnd` event** (`settings.json` registers only UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PermissionDenied/Stop/SessionStart/PreCompact). `Stop` is per-turn; `/wrap` fires only when Erez types the phrase. So "airtight at session end" = "Erez remembers to type two words" — weaker than the dependency we set out to remove.
- Also flagged: secret scan never wired into the highest-risk (new-location) path; a mid-loop crash of the backup step would report success while skipping files.

**Pivot (design direction, NOT built):** reviewers converged on **continuous backup as work happens** (a PostToolUse hook on writes) **+ a SessionStart catch-up** that reconciles each repo against what's actually backed up using git's own truth (`git status`), not a custom log. Keep the fail-closed secret scan and the no-auto-repo guard.

**Ground truth verified live this session:** all 3 projects are git repos w/ GitHub remotes, clean + pushed, no untracked non-ignored files (only `node_modules` ignored); **project work is backed up ONLY by `git push` at `/wrap`** — NOT in any continuous-sync folder; `C:\Users\Erez\AI Projects` is a plain local dir (not OneDrive, not a link into `G:`); `.claude` is backed up because `sync.ps1` explicitly COPIES it to `G:` + the git-history repo; **git works on the `G:` Drive mount** (init/add/commit/status clean in a temp folder, since deleted) BUT `G:` is a streamed drive flagged risky for live repos; **path-migration cost inventoried** — ~170 files mention the path but nearly all are historical transcripts that don't break; live refs needing edits = global `CLAUDE.md`, `settings.local.json`, `loghistory.md`, `gen292-verify/SKILL.md`, each project's `CLAUDE.md`, Drive-tooling scripts, several of them LOCKED config files.

**OPEN DECISION (Erez said "not sure" — this is the pickup point).** (a) relocate projects to `G:\My Drive\AI Projects` (Erez's initial pick — leans on Drive continuous sync, but live repos on a streamed drive = real reliability risk + locked-file migration) vs. (b) keep projects on `C:` and build the git-based continuous backup + SessionStart catch-up (**Claude's recommendation after verifying the trade-offs** — avoids both the streamed-drive risk and the migration; git+GitHub already gives the offsite continuous backup (a) would). Full handoff (all decisions, findings, the failed design + why, ground truth, the open decision) is appended onto **GEN-382**; the v1 (pre-revision) design spec is in the session scratchpad (`backup-airtight-design.md`).

**Next session:** resolve (a) vs (b) first; then build the chosen mechanism; then re-`/check` the concrete design before applying, and `/vet-code` for any hook/script (guarded infra).

**GEN-58:** logged a Class-D recurrence ("Designed on an unverified primitive," → 46x, dated trace on Vol. 4 + index bump, both verified via REST) — the first design was built on two untested primitives, one of which the artifact itself flagged as unverified yet still went to `/check`. Caught pre-build, no damage.

**Transient note:** the auto-mode classifier was briefly "temporarily unavailable" mid-session (opus-4-8 classifier path), blocking two read-only checks; both succeeded on retry. Not a credential denial, not the GEN-316 condition — handled silently.

## 2026-07-08 (7) — GEN-377: characterized the stale notion-fetch cache and built a staleness-warning hook

Session on project 3 (Improve AI Infra), Opus 4.8. Erez asked to work GEN-377 and wanted guiding questions or a converged plan up front.

**What GEN-377 was.** A capture ticket (filed at the (3) wrap) to investigate the stale `notion-fetch` MCP cache seen during GEN-372: the tool served a day-old snapshot of GEN-58 pages (`as of 2026-07-07 17:25`) on every fresh call, missing live edits. Questions: nature of the cache, when it invalidates / can be forced fresh, and whether a standing guard is needed.

**Plan, `/check`-converged (3 rounds).** Opened by verifying current state: the bug was NOT reproducing at session start (fresh fetch stamped current), so this began as a forensic investigation. Erez chose option A (characterize + guard now) provided B (root-cause depth) stays reliably re-enterable without him remembering. The plan panel killed my first "durable self-suppressing daily watch" design: the scheduled-task infra here is NOT an autonomous daemon (all 3 existing tasks are reminder-prompts that fire into a live session), a silent watch reintroduces false-silence, and it's disproportionate given a proven REST workaround. **Mid-`/check` I fed the panel a wrong "verified from primary source" claim** (that `gen292-verify` proves a scheduled task can run the local curl+Credential-Manager path — it only proves Apps-Script-cloud access); the panel caught it. Logged as a GEN-58 Class-A recurrence (a capability claim dressed as "verified" fed into a `/check` brief — direct sibling of the existing `[/check reviewer-model premise]` recurrence). Converged answer: no mechanism autonomously catches this without a session open; the durable re-entry is the guard itself carrying the trigger.

**Characterization (bug REPRODUCED live this session).** Controlled REST-vs-MCP probes on GEN-58 Vol. 4: (1) **REST reads live** — append a block → immediate REST re-read shows it + advanced `last_edited_time` (verified twice; this was the load-bearing assumption the panel flagged). (2) **`notion-fetch` reads are served from a lagging cache** — 3 consecutive fetches returned identical `as of 15:23:22.580Z` to the millisecond while REST advanced 15:23→15:39→15:40; the `as of` field is the snapshot time, not live. (3) **Refinement via an MCP-write control:** an MCP write refreshes the cache (stamp jumped to 15:45) but a REST/out-of-band write does not — so "pinned at first fetch, immune to all edits" (my round-1 claim) was WRONG; it's a lagging cache that DOES advance over time (a later read showed 19:12, then 21:03) and misses out-of-band edits. Findings written to [notion-fetch-cache-staleness.md](notes/notion-fetch-cache-staleness.md).

**Guard built (Erez chose C: hook + note).** A `PostToolUse` hook [notion-fetch-staleness.js](C:\Users\Erez\.claude\hooks\notion-fetch-staleness.js) matched to the exact `notion-fetch` tool: on each read it parses the `as of` stamp + page id, reads the Notion token from Credential Manager, does one live REST `GET /v1/pages/{id}`, and injects a warning via `additionalContext` when the snapshot trails live `last_edited_time` by ≥60s. Fires on every read; fails silent on any error (only ever ADDS a warning, never blocks, never false-alarms). **Confirmed the real PostToolUse input shape** via a scratchpad bootstrap-log (field is `tool_response`, an array of `{type,text}`), then removed the logging. **Verified end-to-end:** forced-stale fixture → correct warning; fresh → silent; syntax clean; **and it FIRED IN PRODUCTION this session** (caught a stale epic fetch: `2026-06-02` snapshot vs live `2026-07-08 19:51`). Wired across all 3 config locations: added to `sync.ps1` manifest, copied to Drive + git-history (byte-identical, SHA-verified), registered in `settings.json` via the locked-file `update-config.ps1` path (JSON validated). A documentation note added to [notion.md](C:\Users\Erez\.claude\hooks\refs\notion.md) covering what the hook can't (sub-agent gap; warn-not-block; page-level `last_edited_time` verified-for-top-level-inferred-for-nested). Hook+note `/check`-converged (2 rounds): the panel confirmed page `last_edited_time` bumps on block appends (so the GEN-372 append case IS covered), and forced a wording softening from "you'll be told" (overclaim) to "usually … a backstop, not a guarantee."

**Outcome.** [GEN-377](https://app.notion.com/p/3976e495d07c81e2895ac481f7bb85a7) → **Done** (primary ticket; hook verified in-session and live-fired; the hook activates for other sessions at their session start). Filed [GEN-388](https://app.notion.com/p/3976e495d07c8188ae13e5a385403fed) (upgrade the hook to auto-refetch-and-replace fresh content instead of warn-only — the pre-vetted next step if warnings get ignored). GEN-58 Class-A bumped 21x→22x (the mid-`/check` verified-claim recurrence). Project-folder edits this session: `notes/notion-fetch-cache-staleness.md` (created + edited).
